references.text: The magicians of Egypt also performed signs with their secret arts, showing that they repeatedly tried to imitate the miracles of Moses and Aaron.
The magicians repeated this pattern by producing frogs with their secret arts.
The magicians tried to produce gnats but could not, and had to admit that this was the finger of God.
The Lord had predicted that he would harden Pharaoh's heart so that he would not let the people go.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said.
Through the plagues, the Lord repeatedly hardened Pharaoh's heart, fulfilling his word.
Paul mentions Jannes and Jambres as those who opposed Moses, traditionally identified as Egyptian magicians.
The Lord had predicted that he would harden Pharaoh's heart and that Pharaoh would not listen to them.
Deep insight into the nature of hardening: Even recognizing God's finger does not change Pharaoh's stubbornness.
Contrasting mechanism: Pharaoh's own active hardening during periods of relief versus his reaction to signs.
Conclusion on the process of hardening: Confirms that the prophecy about Pharaoh's stubbornness was fully fulfilled.
Clear allusion: Uses the story of Pharaoh as a warning example in a new context.
Consequence of hardening: Shows how stubbornness escalates from resistance to military pursuit.
Theological consistency: Confirms that God's action of making the heart hard continues throughout the time of the plagues.
Theological parallel: Uses Pharaoh's hardened heart as an image of human sin and stubbornness in general.
